- Terraform: provider & lifecycle hooks for physical BGP peers, cross-connects, and private CIDR mapping
- Helm: gateway values schema, TLS secret handling, and service annotations for internal load balancer
- Ansible: idempotent bond/mtu config and SR-IOV NIC binding steps

Can we schedule a 60m technical walk-through? Suggested times: Wed 11/18 16:00-17:00 PT or Thu 11/19 morning PT. If helpful, we'll send a short patch with suggested TF state layout.

Agenda (proposed):

I pulled the repo and sketched a few quick comments — forwarding inline to keep the thread intact. I also attached a tiny diff (gateway-module-diff.patch) that suggests a Helm values change and an Ansible handler to make the NIC binding safe on repeat runs.

On Wed, Nov 17, 2026 at 10:08 AM Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the diagram and the clear agenda. We can run a deep-dive on Wed 11/18 at 16:00 PT; that works for the infra team. I'll drop a calendar invite.
> 
> Pre-reads we'd appreciate before the call (short bullets):
> - TF module README and inputs/outputs (a short module-level state diagram if available)
> - Helm values schema and any templating conventions you rely on (secrets, annotations)
> - CI job snippet that deploys the stack (we want to look for non-idempotent steps)

Marcus' notes (high-level):
- Terraform:
  * Do not rely on local-exec for peering setups — move to a provider-native resource where possible. local-exec breaks plan/apply determinism and makes drift detection unreliable.
  * State layout: prefer a separate state per physical site (module per-site) so we can run targeted imports and avoid cross-site locking.
  * Lifecycle prevents accidental destroy: only use create_before_destroy on resources with safe replacement semantics; don't blanket apply on all network resources.
- Helm:
  * Recommend splitting TLS secret provisioning out of the chart: expect the chart to accept a sealed secret or existing KMS-backed secret reference. Don't bake cert generation into pre-install hooks.
  * Values: add explicit annotation map for internal LB provider flags — currently values.yaml flattens provider hints into templated strings which complicates CI validation.
- Ansible:
  * Add a pre-flight check for SR-IOV capability and bail with a clear error message; idempotency must be verified with 'changed' semantics only when a real change occurs.
  * Handler approach in the attached patch toggles bond only when necessary; avoids transient interface flaps that impact cluster control plane.

I'll open a small PR with the patch (attached). If Alex can share the CI job snippet before the call, I can point to exact gate assertions we'd add (terraform fmt/tfsec/tfplan checks, helm template dry-run validations, and ansible --check smoke tests).

--
Marcus Lin

- CI gating (Irene + Marcus + Karthik): Add a tfplan gate and a helm template validation in CI; Marcus to publish a CI archetype PR and Karthik will validate provider permission scoping by 2026-11-22.
- Ansible idempotency (Alex + Marcus): Apply the attached handler pattern; Alex to run an ansible --check test and share results.
